newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Sweden does not yet qualify for EMU - Dutch finmin.
newsitem.headline: Sweden does not yet qualify for EMU - Dutch finmin.

text.p: Dutch Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm said on Monday Sweden did not now qualify for monetary union even if it wanted to join as it was not a member of the bloc's exchange rate mechanism (ERM).

"At this moment it couldn't even join if it wanted to," Zalm told Reuters. Zalm, chairing a meeting of EU finance ministers in Luxembourg, was asked to comment on the decision by the party board of Sweden's ruling Social Democrats last week that Sweden would not join EMU at its planned 1999 start.
Zalm said the other ministers had "taken note" of the Swedish decision. Asked whether there had been a discussion about Stockholm's position, he said: "Not really."

"It is a political fact and at this moment Sweden would not qualify for EMU because it is not a member of the exchange rate mechanism," Zalm added. "If they would ask now they would be rejected because they are not (a) member of ERM."
Sweden says currency stability and not formal ERM membership should determine whether a country qualifies for EMU.
However, several EU countries, including Germany and France, insist ERM membership is a requirement.

The Social Democrat's party board said last week its decision to stay out from the start, expected to be confirmed by parliament later this year, was largely due to widespread public opposition to EMU. But it left the door open to join at a later date.
